families.axis: killing softened into slang or euphemism → killing named outright as murder

members.tone: The flat, full-weight name for the act, leaving the premeditation showing where *dispatch* and *remove* tidy it out of sight.
Elevated and grave where *off* is curt, giving a planned killing a weight of ceremony rather than condemning it.
Slang that treats a premeditated killing as a job done, the coolness of the word doing the work *murder* does with weight.
Brisk and efficient, filing the killing under business concluded rather than under wrongdoing.
Slang with a shrug in it, making the killing offhand and almost comic in a way *slay* never allows.
One cold slang syllable, the deliberate act shrunk to a word too small to hold it.
Informal and jaunty, its air of finishing a task neatly is exactly what makes it callous here.
The furthest euphemism in the set, rendering a premeditated killing as an act of tidying and hiding the intent inside the blandness.
Names the killing by its method, leaving no mark on the body, and is chilling precisely because it is that specific where *murder* is general.
members._gloss: murder without leaving a trace on the body

members.tone: Lends a planned murder the cold air of sentence carried out, borrowing an authority the act does not have.
The plain word of the family, giving confidence or faith directly, with none of the reckoning *calculate* brings or the staking *bet* brings.
Aims the trust at whether a thing is true rather than whether it will hold, granting belief where *lean* grants weight.
members._gloss: have trust in; trust in the truth or veracity of

members.tone: Casts the reliance as bodily weight put on a support, carrying the hint that the one leaning could not stand unaided.
Treats the confidence as already entered in the tally, so the thing believed in is settled rather than merely hoped for.
Frames the faith as a stake laid down, conceding in the same breath that it could be lost, where *rely* concedes nothing of the kind.
The confidence has need underneath it, with nothing else holding the one who depends upright.
Emphatic to the point of vouching, the faith declared aloud rather than quietly kept as in *rely*.
Steady and unemphatic: confidence as a standing arrangement rather than the wager *bet* makes of it.
Puts the faith down like a deposit, everything in one place and nothing held back.
The faintest of the set, confidence as expectation turned toward a thing without the weight *lean* or *bank* place on it.
Makes the confidence the outcome of working something out, so it sounds arrived at rather than felt.
Informal, stating the faith as a settled count, plainer than *swear* and less deliberate than *calculate*.
Settled and unhedged - the trust is already placed and resting there, with none of the risk still audible in *bet* and none of the need implied by *lean*.
The weightier, more formal cast of *depend on*, claiming exactly the same confident placing of trust.
Trust placed with assurance, active and chosen where *depend on* keeps the note of need.
Formal beside *rely on*, the same confident placing of trust carried with a stiffer bearing.
The plainest way of holding something high, without the warmth of *admire* or the hush of *revere*.
Formal and cool: high regard delivered as an assessment rather than a felt rush.
Casts the high regard as worth — what the thing is worth to the holder, not what it stirs in them.
The regard of someone who would not part with it; more possessive than *value*.
Carries the treasuring force of *prize* exactly, under a different spelling.
Idiomatic and whole-hearted, an open overstatement where *esteem* keeps its measure.
Lifts the object past approval into the hallowed, met with awe rather than judged.
members._gloss: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe o

members.tone: The member in which awe keeps its edge of dread — respect owed to something too exalted to face lightly.
members._gloss: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe o

members.tone: The felt act of reverence, awe aimed at what is held sacred, far past *respect*.
members._gloss: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe o

members.tone: Treats the object as hallowed, the regard almost ceremonial where *admire* is simply warm.
members._gloss: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe o

members.tone: A felt response to something, where *esteem* is a verdict on it.
Admiration that puts the object above the one feeling it; plainer and more informal than *venerate*.

families.axis: sadness felt on one's own account → suffering deliberately taken on with another

members.tone: The plain full-weight word for grief felt as grief, neither approving nor blaming the one who feels it.
Makes the grief sound inward and sustained where *grieve* sounds like something done.
On this sense it asks only for sadness, short of the weight *grieve* insists on.
Warm and plain-spoken, the sharing conveyed with none of the formality of *condole with*.
Shares the suffering from slightly above it, so the warmth carries a downward tilt that *sympathize with* has not.
The most morally weighted here - sharing the suffering treated as a virtue exercised, and stiff enough as a verb to sound elevated.
Formal and ceremonious - the sharing is performed toward the sufferer rather than merely felt.
The mildest of the sharing words, acknowledging and joining the suffering at conversational temperature.
